text:
nina: Ran a flutter/iOS sample under heavy network churn and observed chunks arriving out-of-order after an auth refresh + parallel reconnects. This looks different from the usual final-chunk-loss issue. The client ends up applying tokens in wrong order -> garbled final output.

rahul: can you paste the minimal log? is this happening with proxy enabled or direct-hosted API?

nina: repro uses our mobile sample behind the rdp proxy (dedicated pool). repro steps: start 30s streaming generation, shorten token TTL to force refresh at ~20s, simulate flaky 100ms network blips so the mobile client issues a reconnection while a background reconnect attempt is already in-flight. Logs: 

```
SERVER: send chunk seq=10 payload="token-A" flags=CONT
SERVER: send chunk seq=11 payload="token-B" flags=CONT
SERVER: send chunk seq=12 payload="token-C" flags=CONT
PROXY: client conn A -> backend req x (seq 10..12)
PROXY: backend connection transiently slow, proxy opens backend req y as retry for client conn B
CLIENT: recv seq=10
CLIENT: recv seq=12
CLIENT: recv seq=11
```

pat: whoa. That implies proxy retried a request and merged responses from two backend connections, or the client replayed an in-flight range. Both are bad. Does the proxy layer do per-chunk ordering guarantees?

nina: proxy is supposed to be transparent. It has connection pooling + retry for idempotent requests, but streaming requests are flagged non-idempotent; however, during the reconnect dance the mobile SDK started two parallel fetches briefly (race on auth refresh), and the proxy's retry logic accepted both and interleaved frames.

miles: interesting. Two angles: SDK should prevent concurrent streaming fetches for same logical session (dedupe recon attempts), and runtime/proxy shouldn't interleave multiple backends for one client stream. We probably need both.

rahul: SDK change: single-flight streaming connect per session id + cancel older attempt gracefully. Also add a short jittered backoff before re-opening to avoid head-of-line races. That should reduce client-side concurrency.

pat: runtime/proxy change: ensure per-stream ordering by attaching a monotonic connection id and sequence gating in proxy. If proxy sees chunks from two backend connections for same client stream, it should buffer and reorder based on seq number, or reject the second connection instead of merging. Buffering could increase memory but safer.

nina: another observation: resume tokens are based on "last stable token index" which maps to payload token offsets, not chunk sequence. When chunks are re-ordered we can't make sense of resume semantics. We need chunk-level seqs surfaced in resume tokens (or multi-dimensional resume tokens: seq + tokenIndex + byteOffset).

miles: agreed. Proposal: extend resume token to include the last_received_seq and last_received_token_idx. Server will accept resume requests of form resume_from_seq=N and only stream subsequent seq> N. That makes retries simple.

rahul: backwards compatibility concern: older SDKs will send token-only resume. We can support either: resume token with seq if present, else fall back to token index. But then runtime must be careful re: duplicate content when seq absent.

pat: short-term mitigations:
- SDK: single-flight connect + 200ms grace window before spawning a reconnect (opt-in flag mobile-sample.graceOnAuthMs)
- Proxy: disable automatic retry-on-connection-failure for streaming endpoints (config flip)
- Devex: add a mobile parity test that simulates concurrent reconnect attempts and asserts chunk monotonicity

dev-bot: Created task DEVEX-2301 and linked to runtime ticket ENG-RT-4819.

nina: I'll open PR in mobile-sample for single-flight connect and a small grace jitter. Will add integration test that replays packet traces.

rahul: I'll prototype proxy gating logic (buffer+reorder by seq, with memory cap + fallback to reject). If we can't keep memory low, we should prefer rejecting second backend connection and returning 409-like handshake error to client so client retries cleanly.

miles: please also record telemetry for "duplicate concurrent streams per session" so we can measure how often SDK hits this. Add warning logs when proxy sees multiple connections for same stream id.

pat: good call. We should also update our SDK docs to discourage concurrent streaming attempts and show best practice for auth refresh (rotate token in place without tearing the fetch where possible).

nina: thanks all. I'll file the mobile-sample PR and attach the failing pcap. Linking DEVEX-2301 here.

rahul: follow-up: once we have seq-aware resume token, we can simplify server retry semantics; up to runtime to implement. Marking this P0 for parity tests.

miles: thumbs up. Let's track in ENG-RT-4819 and circle back after initial proxy POC.

nina: thanks team. I'll post stress-run results in this thread. :rocket:
